grh_b72db493fb787eea00eb.title: The Big Lift
paragraphs: American airmen Hank and Danny are sent into the Berlin Airlift, flying food and supplies into a city cut off by the Soviet blockade. Hank is openly suspicious of Germans after the war, while Danny becomes romantically involved with Frederica, a young German woman whose ruined city and uncertain future awaken his sympathy. Their experiences gradually force both men to look beyond wartime labels and confront what occupation, defeat, and democracy mean in everyday life. Danny proposes to Frederica, only to discover a letter revealing that she has been using him as a path to the United States while planning to reunite with another man there. Hurt, he breaks off the marriage. Hank, meanwhile, learns from Gerta that democracy includes the freedom to challenge authority, and both airmen leave Berlin with a more complicated understanding of the people they had first judged so simply.

grh_b78188decf84430a0456.title: Alias Nick Beal
paragraphs: Idealistic district attorney Joseph Foster is desperate to convict racketeer Hanson when mysterious Nick Beal offers him the evidence he needs. Each favor draws Foster deeper into compromise: forged books win the case, political influence carries him toward the governor's office, and Beal plants glamorous Donna Allen beside him while gradually isolating him from his wife and conscience. Foster finally realizes Beal's bargains amount to a claim on his soul. After resigning the governorship rather than serve the corrupt interests that elected him, Foster is still bound by a written contract requiring him to follow Beal. Reverend Garfield places the agreement inside a Bible, which Beal cannot take, breaking his hold. Foster is saved, while Beal withdraws to wait for other people willing to make the same bargain.
